The OpenAI models that broke out of their test environment are fueling “long term questions” about how AI companies should address this new rate of progress. [...] The letter comes on the heels of major advancements and burgeoning threats from rapidly developing AI systems. items.title: Jim Cramer says Wall Street is fleeing the AI trade and buying these stocks instead
items.summary:
"The stocks just anticipate the ending," he added.

Take Western Digital, the stock hit an all-time closing high of $746 per share on June 18 — at the time, up 333% for the year. Less than six weeks later, the stock is down nearly 40% from its record.

Cramer stressed, however, that investors are not abandoning the market altogether. Instead, they are redeploying capital into companies whose growth depends less on continued AI infrastructure spending. [...] Prime examples are Micron, Western Digital, Seagate, and Sandisk, whose shares soared as shortages of memory used in AI servers gave the companies unprecedented pricing power. After peaking in June, those stocks have tumbled as investors bet those shortages — and the extraordinary profits they created — won't last forever.

"I have been through many boom-bust cycles with these companies," Cramer said. "You have to sell the parabolic moves that these shortages trigger because they always end." [...] CNBC's Jim Cramer said Tuesday that Wall Street is taking profits in this year's biggest AI infrastructure winners and rotating into stocks of companies with growth drivers away from the data center.

"You can call it a broadening," the "Mad Money" host said. "Or you can call it fleeing."

Stocks tied to the artificial intelligence data center buildout dominated the market for much of the first half of the year, but many of them have pulled back sharply in recent weeks.

items.title: Developing Healthcare Robotics with GPU-Native Medical Physics Simulation
items.summary:
Healthcare robotics faces critical challenges in data scarcity, generalization, and development velocity due to limited access to annotated demonstrations, the prevalence of rare but clinically important scenarios, and slow, resource-intensive prototyping cycles. [...] AI-generated content may summarize information incompletely. Verify important information. Learn more

Unlike autonomous driving or industrial robotics, healthcare robotics can’t rely on internet-scale data collection or unlimited real-world experimentation. Every demonstration requires specialized equipment, clinical expertise, and access to patients or laboratory environments. This creates three fundamental challenges for developers. [...] The third challenge is development velocity. Medical robotics development relies on benchtop phantoms, cadaver studies, animal models, and limited clinical evaluations. These remain essential, but they are inherently sequential, expensive, and difficult to scale. Iterating on designs and algorithms currently takes months, pushing total development cycles to 4–7 years.

items.title: FCC bans humanoid robots from China, citing ‘unacceptable risks’

items.title: OpenAI's $1 Trillion IPO Ambition Faces New Timing Test as Anthropic Gains Ground - Dailyhunt
items.summary: **OpenAI** may be pushing back its public debut as it weighs whether market conditions can support its reported goal of a $1 trillion valuation. The analysts noted that OpenAI's decision on timing effectively acts as a pricing signal: management must choose between going public sooner at a potentially discounted valuation or waiting longer in hopes of reaching the $1 trillion mark. Despite OpenAI's higher valuation (private market valuations of $852 billion), PitchBook ($965 billion) suggested Anthropic currently commands a more attractive valuation relative to its business quality score. PitchBook said investors should watch for OpenAI to convert its confidential filing into a public S-1, the pricing of its employee tender offer, SpaceX’s Aug. 6 earnings and lockup timeline, and whether Anthropic proceeds with an October IPO. The firm said its outlook would change if OpenAI moves ahead with a 2026 IPO or if its public S-1 shows investors are willing to support a $1 trillion valuation sooner than expected.

items.title: OpenAI's rogue models roamed the internet for 4 days and staged a second attack - Politico
items.summary: GLOBAL POLITICS & POLICY 4 items. A second AI company confirmed that one of its customers was also targeted by OpenAI’s models. The powerful artificial intelligence models from OpenAI that went rogue and mounted an unprecedented, autonomous cyberattack earlier this month spent more than four days loose on the internet orchestrating the hack, according to a new analysis from the platform that was breached. Separately, a second AI company confirmed that one of its customers was also targeted by OpenAI’s models during the same event, raising questions about how OpenAI failed to detect the alarming activity for days. But in a new analysis published Tuesday, Hugging Face said OpenAI’s two models — one publicly released and a second unreleased — did much more: They carried out 17,600 hacking actions on the internet between July 9 and July 13, during which time the models moved from their first foothold on the open internet to inside Hugging Face’s servers.

items.title: AI cyberattacks are coming? OpenAI experiment sparks new security debate - Ynetnews
items.summary: ## OpenAI’s AI agent experiment, which demonstrated an autonomous simulated cyber operation in a controlled environment, has intensified debate over how AI could reshape future cyberattacks as systems gain greater ability to plan and execute complex tasks. An OpenAI experiment in which an AI agent autonomously escaped a sandboxed environment and carried out a multi-step offensive operation has intensified a growing debate in the cybersecurity community: Are AI-powered cyberattacks already moving from theory into reality? The experiment was conducted in a controlled setting and was not a real-world attack. But security experts say it demonstrated a significant shift in the capabilities of AI systems — not because the model discovered a vulnerability, something AI tools have done before, but because it was able to independently plan and execute a sequence of actions resembling an end-to-end attack. Roie Cohen Duwek, CTO of Surf AI, said the most important lesson from the experiment was not the discovery of a single vulnerability, but the ability to coordinate an entire attack chain.

items.title: OpenAI Plans to Spend Over $30 Billion on Georgia Data Center - Insurance Journal
items.summary: # OpenAI Plans to Spend Over $30 Billion on Georgia Data Center. OpenAI plans to spend tens of billions of dollars on a massive new data center near Savannah, Georgia as part of the ChatGPT maker’s push to keep up with surging demand for artificial intelligence software. The startup has contracted with Georgia Power Co. and secured 3.2 gigawatts of energy for the data center complex in Effingham County, potentially setting the facility up to rank among OpenAI’s largest to date. OpenAI committed to spend $20 billion in the county in order to qualify for an incentive package that will be voted on this week, the company said. The startup is currently looking for partners to help finance and develop the data center, Katti said, and may opt to do some of the operation itself. The company has partnered with developers on large data centers in Europe, the Middle East and several US states as part of its Stargate initiative.
